summary: Tougher and more flexible than PLA. Snaps tolerate about 2 to 4 % strain. Takes about 70–80 °C. Strings, and oozes slightly fatter than PLA.
clearance_note: PLA defaults + 0.05 per side, because PETG prints slightly fatter; replace them with values measured on your printer (processed/fits-PETG.json)
slicer: good layer bonding for snaps and latches
textured PEI, or smooth PEI with glue stick / release agent
PETG can bond to smooth PEI and tear it
do not squish PETG: elephant foot closes bed-side holes and grooves
outer walls 30 mm/s, inner 50 mm/s, infill 60 mm/s
slow outer walls keep the fits true
30–50 %, off for the first 3 layers, 100 % on bridges
too much fan weakens PETG layer bonds
direct drive 0.8–1.0 mm @ 35 mm/s, Bowden 4–5 mm @ 40 mm/s; wipe on, avoid crossing perimeters
PETG strings, and strings jam fits and hinges
0.2 mm (turn it off if stringing gets worse)
rear / aligned, away from snaps, latches and hinges
a seam blob changes a click
notes: Dry the filament before printing (65 °C for 4–6 h). Wet PETG strings, pops and prints rough fits.
Clean strings off pins, holes and grooves before assembly (a hot blade or a quick pass with a heat gun).
If a fit is too tight, first lower the flow by 2 %, then raise the clearance in processed/fits-PETG.json and finalize again.
